opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
The blind man asked to see, and Christ gave him sight. But what Christ declared over him was greater: “Your faith has saved you.” The physical healing and salvation are connected, but not identical. One healed his eyes; the other spoke to eternity.

Jesus could have simply restored his vision and said, “Now you can see, go on.” But He did not. Instead, He interprets the miracle itself. Almost as though Christ is saying: you came asking for one thing, but something much larger happened here.

And after receiving sight, the blind man does not truly go his own way — he follows Jesus. The healing becomes discipleship.

You wonder if the blind man even understood what happened in that moment. Imagine seeing for the first time after darkness while simultaneously hearing Christ declare salvation over you. Perhaps he was overwhelmed.

The blind man wanted sight. Christ gave him sight, salvation, and Himself. Faith opened more than the eyes. It opened the possibility of communion with God. Not merely a restored life, but entrance into the life Christ continually points toward — the Father, in whom there are many dwellings.
